entities.summary: Frederic Clemson Howe was a progressive era reform politician and author who served one term as a member of the Ohio Senate (1903–1907) before becoming managing director of the People's Institute in New York City in 1910 and Commissioner of Immigration of the Port of New York in 1914. He was also founder and president of the League of Small and Subject Nationalities.
